title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is section d) of the notes, which begins on the previous page: 'Application à la structure de M_{ρ,σ} et à la définition d'un hom. M → M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ'. The setting is profinite groups attached to the genus-0 / modular-tower picture.
- M is a profinite group, written M = M(0)·S^{+∧}, with M(0) ≃ M_{0,3}(0).
- G_{ρ,σ} ≃ M.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} = G_{ρ,σ}/S^{+∧} ≃ Π_Q^~, an (extended) absolute Galois group of Q.
- ρ and σ are the two special points, presumably the elliptic points of orders 3 and 2 of the modular curve. L_ρ and L_σ are their local (inertia/stabilizer) subgroups.
- N*_ρ = Norm_M(L_ρ) and N*_σ = Norm_M(L_σ) play the role of decomposition groups.
- M_{ρ,σ} = N*_ρ ×_Γ N*_σ ×_Γ G_{ρ,σ}, a fibre product over the Galois quotient (eq. 48).
- From the previous page: Z^!_σ = M(1/2) ⊂ N*_σ maps isomorphically onto Γ, and Z^!_σ ∩ μ = 1. Also N^?_ρ = Z^!_ρ·μ ⊂ N*_ρ is a central extension 1 → μ → N^?_ρ → Γ → 1. Here μ is a small central subgroup, presumably μ_2 = {±1}.

On this page:
(53) Grothendieck defines the subgroup M^⇆_{ρ,σ} = N^?_ρ ×_Γ Z^!_σ ×_Γ G_{ρ,σ} ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}. These are the 'privileged' sub-decomposition groups at ρ and σ: rational sections or tangential-base-point-type lifts.
(54) The three central copies of μ (in N*_ρ, N*_σ and G ⊂ G^+) all lie over 1 in Γ. Together they give a central embedding μ×μ×μ ↪ M_{ρ,σ}.
- He then intersects with M^⇆. Since Z^!_σ ∩ μ = 1, only the σ-component is killed. With the factor order (ρ, σ, G) the intersection should therefore be μ×1×μ. The text writes (1×μ×μ), which is a slip; the next page indeed says the intersection with SZ_ρ×SZ_σ is μ_ρ×1.
(55) This gives μ×μ ↪ M^⇆. Write μ_ρ for the copy μ×1×1.
(55') Projecting onto the third factor gives an exact sequence 1 → μ_ρ → M^⇆_{ρ,σ} → G_{ρ,σ} (≃ M) → 1. Check:
- Kernel: elements (n, z, 1) with n, z over 1 ∈ Γ. Then z = 1, because Z^!_σ ≅ Γ, and n ∈ ker(N^?_ρ → Γ) = μ.
- Surjectivity: every g ∈ G has image in Γ, which lifts uniquely to Z^!_σ and (non-uniquely) to N^?_ρ.
The page ends with 'd'où des homomorphismes canoniques'. The next page gives (56): M ≃ M^⇆/μ_ρ ↪ M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ.

Purpose: realise the full group M as a subgroup of (a quotient of) the fibre product of the two decomposition groups. Equivalently, produce a canonical 'bisection' of Γ_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}, i.e. a simultaneous Galois-equivariant splitting at the two elliptic points, modulo the central sign ambiguity μ_ρ. This is a step in Grothendieck's study of the Galois action on the profinite modular/Teichmüller groupoid via the 'équation des lacets'.
errors: The intersection M^⇆ ∩ (μ×μ×μ) is written (1×μ×μ). Given Z^!_σ ∩ μ = 1 (eq. 51) and N^?_ρ ⊃ μ, with the factor order (ρ, σ, G) it should be μ×1×μ. This matches the next page ('intersection … est μ_ρ×1') and the subsequent use of μ_ρ as the kernel.
The fibre products on this page are subscripted with γ_{ρ,σ}, whereas (48) uses Γ_{ρ,σ}. The notation is fluid between pages.

ideas.what: Subgroup of the fibre product of decomposition groups (normalizers of the inertia at ρ and σ) over the Galois quotient, built from privileged sections Z^!_σ ≅ Γ and the central extension N^?_ρ
ideas.modern_name: Galois sections / tangential base points at the elliptic points of the profinite modular group; GT-type compatibility of decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura (Galois action on π1 of M_{1,1} / modular curves), Deligne (tangential base points), Drinfeld (GT)
ideas.where_published: The general programme is in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (1981). This specific construction appears to be only in these archive notes.

ideas.what: Central extension 1 → μ_ρ → M^⇆ → M → 1, giving a canonical embedding M ↪ M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ and a 'bisection' of Γ_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: Simultaneous lifting of Galois sections at two cusps/elliptic points modulo a central sign (±1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related to Nakamura's and Ihara's work on the Galois action on profinite SL2(Z)/PSL2(Z) and on GT

missed.claim: The page shows an unpublished, detailed group-theoretic device: the full Teichmüller-type group M embeds into the fibre product of the decomposition groups at the two elliptic points ρ and σ, modulo a central μ. Equivalently, there is a simultaneous splitting ('bisection') of the Galois action at both elliptic points. This is part of Grothendieck's unpublished analysis of the loop equation for the modular tower. On its own the page is routine homological bookkeeping.
missed.quote: 1 → μ_ρ ↪ M^⇆_{ρ,σ} → G_{ρ,σ} → 1 ; ≀ M ; d'où des homomorphismes canoniques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may be of interest for comparison with Nakamura's, Ihara's and Hoshi–Mochizuki-style work on Galois sections at elliptic points of M_{1,1} and on the anabelian structure of the profinite modular group. The page itself contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical, correct (up to a factor-order slip) step building a canonical homomorphism by fibre products and central extensions. It belongs to an unpublished programme on the Galois action at elliptic points, which is of some historical interest, but the page contains no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: In (53) the first factor appears to be N^?_ρ (an N overwritten, with a '?' superscript), consistent with (50)–(52), not Z^?_ρ.
The fraction-like 'G_{ρ,σ}/M' in (53) is G_{ρ,σ} with '≃ M' written underneath it, not a quotient.
Below the arrow μ ↪ G_{ρ,σ}, the curved arrow reads ↪ G^+_{ρ,σ} = G^+ (with an arrow G^+ → G_{ρ,σ}).
'Il est clair alors par (52)': the reference (52) is legible enough.
